note: Who may authorise a data correction or revert (DI-03F, hardened DI-04). Identity is a SIGNING KEY, not a name: an approval is an OpenSSH signature (ssh-keygen -Y sign -n thriv3-correction-approval@v1) over the approval body, verified against the keys enrolled here (server/lib/refresh/approvalValidator.js). One raw key is one person: the same key under two reviewer ids, in any encoding, refuses the whole registry. A SHARED_DEV or PRODUCTION scope needs every key to be an attested hardware key entered as {"key": "sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com ...", "attestation": "<base64>", "challenge": "<base64>"} (made with ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk -O verify-required -O write-attestation -O challenge; procedure in docs/CORRECTION_REVIEWER_SECURITY.md), whose attestation verifies against a root pinned in shared/fidoAttestationRoots.json; approvals for those scopes must carry touch AND PIN/biometric. Changing this file is a T2 change gated by CODEOWNERS, and a correction against a SHARED_DEV or PRODUCTION database refuses if this file differs from origin/main (server/lib/refresh/trustRoot.js). The rehearsal key may never hold a runtime scope. A reviewer with no enrolled key cannot approve anything.
